newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLYGRAM SEES CHARGE OF $90 MLN IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLYGRAM SEES CHARGE OF $90 MLN IN 1996.

text.p: Music and entertainment group PolyGram said its 1996 result will reflect a one time reorganisation charge of $90 million as result of restructuring its music operations.

"Entering the important fourth quarter the company currently expects full year 1996 operating result before restructuring charges to be flat or slightly below last year's, caused by lower than expected music sales," it said in a statement.
PolyGram added it achieved a compound annual growth rate of 11 percent in net sales and 16 percent in net income from 1990-95.
PolyGram said it had been affected by the present sluggish conditions in music markets worldwide.
It has also experienced lower sales than expected of its current releases due to issues specific to PolyGram, which management is addressing through the restructuring, it said.
PolyGram will restructure its label Motown.
It will reorganise its European music distribution and marketing operations in response to the flat market.
It will also restructure the classical music division.
This action will result in about 400 job losses worldwide.
